lineas.texto: Part One. You will hear three different extracts. For each question, choose the answer — A, B or C — which fits best according to what you hear. There are two questions for each extract.
Extract one. You hear two colleagues discussing a report.
Have you had a chance to look at the draft I sent over?
I have, and I'll be honest with you: the findings are solid, but nobody is going to read forty pages of them.
That's rather the point, though. If I cut it down, the first thing to go would be the methodology, and then anyone who disagrees with us has an easy way in.
Put the methodology in an appendix. Nobody reads appendices either, but they can't accuse you of hiding it.
You're probably right. I've been treating length as a sign of seriousness, which is a habit I picked up at university and should have dropped.
We all did. Send me the short version and I'll tell you if it still says what you mean.
Extract two. You hear a woman telling a friend about a course she has started.
I signed up for the pottery class expecting it to relax me, and honestly, for the first month it did the opposite.
Because you weren't any good at it?
Because I couldn't stand not being any good at it. That's not the same thing. At work I've spent thirty years being the person who knows what she's doing.
So what changed?
The teacher stopped me in the middle of the fourth week and said, very kindly, that I was gripping the clay as if it owed me money. And she was right.
And now?
Now I make some genuinely terrible bowls and I don't mind. My husband minds. He has to eat off them.
Extract three. You hear two people discussing a change at their local station.
Did you see they're taking the ticket office out? Machines only from June.
I did. And I know I'm supposed to be furious about it, but I bought my last three tickets on my phone and I couldn't tell you when I last spoke to anyone in there.
That's exactly the argument they're making, and it works right up until you're eighty and the machine won't take your card.
Well, quite. My objection isn't really the machines, it's that they've promised staff will still be on the platform and I don't believe a word of it.
Nor do I. That's always the second cut.
So I'll sign the petition, but I'll sign it about the staff, not about the window.
That is the end of Part One.
